records.title: Type A and Type B describe evaluation methods
records.text: Type A uses statistical evaluation; Type B uses other information. These categories do not map one-to-one onto random and systematic effects.
assumptions: The stated model and source scope apply to the task.
limitations: Do not classify an effect solely by whether it appears random or systematic.

records.title: Standard uncertainty
records.text: Standard uncertainty represents an uncertainty component as an estimated standard deviation.
assumptions: The stated model and source scope apply to the task.
limitations: This reference is not a laboratory calibration or independent replication.

records.title: Error is not uncertainty
records.text: A result can have a small unknown error yet substantial uncertainty. Uncertainty is not the realized error.
assumptions: The stated model and source scope apply to the task.
limitations: The true error is generally not known from an uncertainty estimate.

records.title: Type A methods beyond repeated means
records.text: Type A evaluations can use valid statistical analyses such as least squares or analysis of variance, not only repeated-reading means.
assumptions: The stated model and source scope apply to the task.
limitations: The appropriate statistical design depends on the measurement process.

records.title: Uncertainty of a repeated-reading mean
records.text: For independent observations under the same conditions, estimate the mean uncertainty from their sample dispersion.
assumptions: n >= 2 independent observations under the same measurement conditions.
limitations: Autocorrelation and drift can invalidate this calculation.

records.title: First-order uncertainty propagation
records.text: Combine input variances and covariances using local sensitivities.
assumptions: First-order Taylor approximation; sensitivities evaluated at input estimates.
limitations: Nonlinearity may require another method.

records.title: Correlated measurement inputs
records.text: Covariance terms contribute to the combined variance when inputs are correlated.
assumptions: Covariance estimates describe the joint input uncertainty.
limitations: Zero correlation must not be silently inferred from missing metadata.

records.title: Uncertainty of a difference
records.text: Substituting sensitivities +1 and -1 gives the variance of a difference.
assumptions: Both inputs describe comparable quantities in compatible units.
limitations: No acceptance decision follows without a declared decision rule.

records.title: Type B information sources
records.text: Type B evaluation may use previous data, specifications, calibration reports, experience, and reference information.
assumptions: The stated model and source scope apply to the task.
limitations: A source must be relevant to the actual measurement conditions.

records.title: Uniform bounded uncertainty
records.text: For a symmetric uniform model with half-width a, the standard uncertainty is a divided by sqrt(3).
assumptions: Equal probability within justified symmetric bounds.
limitations: Bounds alone do not establish a uniform distribution.

records.title: Triangular bounded uncertainty
records.text: For a symmetric triangular model with half-width a, use a divided by sqrt(6).
assumptions: A symmetric triangular probability model is justified.
limitations: Do not select this model merely to obtain a smaller uncertainty.

records.title: Convert a reported uncertainty multiplier
records.text: Divide an uncertainty stated as a multiple of a standard deviation by its stated multiplier.
assumptions: The report supplies the multiplier and meaning of U.
limitations: A missing multiplier cannot be guessed.

records.title: Corrections for systematic effects
records.text: Recognized significant systematic effects should be corrected where possible; the correction carries its own uncertainty.
assumptions: The stated model and source scope apply to the task.
limitations: The uncertainty of a correction is not the systematic error itself.

records.title: Combine Type A and Type B components
records.text: Components from either evaluation method enter a combined standard uncertainty with covariance where appropriate.
assumptions: Components use standard uncertainties and a defensible measurement model.
limitations: This reference is not a laboratory calibration or independent replication.

records.title: Expanded uncertainty
records.text: Expanded uncertainty multiplies combined standard uncertainty by a chosen coverage factor.
assumptions: Coverage factor k is explicit and justified.
limitations: Multiplication alone does not establish a coverage probability.

records.title: Coverage factor is not a universal probability
records.text: A factor of two corresponds to approximately 95 percent coverage under the stated normal-distribution and negligible-uncertainty conditions.
assumptions: Normal approximation applies and uncertainty in u_c is negligible for that interpretation.
limitations: Do not label every k=2 interval as 95 percent.

records.title: Report uncertainty with its basis
records.text: Report components, their evaluation methods, and the coverage factor when expanded uncertainty is used. State the basis of any probability interpretation.
assumptions: The stated model and source scope apply to the task.
limitations: Keep referenced measurement procedures consistent with the process used.
TN 1297 section 7 is a historical guidance page marked no longer updated; this is not a current compliance certification.

records.title: Traceability belongs to a measurement result
records.text: Metrological traceability relates a measurement result to a reference through a documented calibration chain with uncertainty contributions.
assumptions: The stated model and source scope apply to the task.
limitations: An instrument calibration by itself does not establish traceability of every subsequent result.

records.title: Traceability documentation requirements
records.text: Document the measurand, measurement system, result and uncertainty, reference calibration, and relevant measurement assurance.
assumptions: The stated model and source scope apply to the task.
limitations: Checking graph links cannot authenticate certificates or establish competence.

records.title: Traceability is not fitness for purpose
records.text: A traceable result can still be unsuitable for an application when its uncertainty is too large.
assumptions: The stated model and source scope apply to the task.
limitations: Application requirements must be evaluated separately.

records.title: Specify the measurand before calculating
records.text: Identify the intended quantity together with the object, state and relevant conditions; a number and an instrument name do not fully specify a measurand.
assumptions: The intended use and object are specified.
limitations: A different condition may define a different measurand, not a repeat of the same measurement.

records.title: Measurement may disturb the target
records.text: Instrument interaction can change the quantity being observed. A justified correction may be needed to estimate the originally intended quantity.
assumptions: The interaction has a defensible measurement model.
limitations: The record does not provide a universal correction for arbitrary instruments.

records.title: Accuracy is not a numerical uncertainty specification
records.text: Accuracy is a qualitative comparison with the quantity value sought. It is not interchangeable with precision or a numerical uncertainty budget.
assumptions: VIM3 terminology is being used.
limitations: A manufacturer label such as accuracy ±x must be interpreted from its stated specification rather than treated as standard uncertainty.

records.title: Precision requires stated measurement conditions
records.text: Replicate dispersion characterizes precision under stated conditions. Standard deviation, variance or a coefficient of variation describes imprecision, not automatically accuracy.
assumptions: Replicates and their operating conditions are identified.
limitations: A small spread does not demonstrate absence of common bias.

records.title: Repeatability conditions
records.text: A repeatability study holds the procedure, operators, system, operating conditions and location fixed over a short period.
assumptions: The scope of what remains unchanged is documented.
limitations: This study alone does not estimate variation across laboratories or long time periods.

records.title: Reproducibility conditions
records.text: A reproducibility study declares which locations, operators, systems or procedures differ and which conditions remain fixed.
assumptions: The same or similar objects and a comparable measurand are used.
limitations: Re-running a software script is not, by itself, metrological reproducibility.

records.title: Uncertainty belongs to the result and information used
records.text: Measurement uncertainty characterizes the dispersion assigned to a result using available information, including appropriate systematic-effect and reference-value components.
assumptions: The measurement model and information set are explicit.
limitations: Repeated-reading scatter is only one potential component.

records.title: Calibration relates standards, indications and results
records.text: Calibration establishes a relationship with standards and uncertainties, then uses that relationship to obtain results from indications.
assumptions: Specified conditions and applicable standards are identified.
limitations: A calibration curve without uncertainty information does not supply a complete result.

records.title: Calibration is not adjustment or verification
records.text: Calibration, changing an instrument response, and checking requirements are distinct operations. Record separately which operation was performed.
assumptions: Operation names are interpreted using VIM3.
limitations: A calibration entry does not automatically mean an instrument was adjusted or passed a tolerance.

records.title: Traceability can involve several input chains
records.text: Multi-input measurements may require a network of calibration chains. Traceability and adequate uncertainty for the intended task are separate questions.
assumptions: The inputs, reference identities and applicable dates are retained.
limitations: A connected document graph does not establish calibration authenticity or fitness for purpose.

records.title: Resolution is not total uncertainty
records.text: Resolution concerns a detectable change in indication and can depend on noise, operating value and mechanism. It does not account for every uncertainty contribution.
assumptions: The instrument and operating conditions are specified.
limitations: Display digits alone do not justify a full uncertainty statement.

records.title: Influence quantity depends on the measurement definition
records.text: A quantity affecting the indication-to-result relationship may be an influence quantity. Object temperature can instead belong to the measurand definition; VIM3 and GUM use different scope here.
assumptions: The vocabulary edition and direct/indirect measurement context are declared.
limitations: Do not merge vocabulary editions into a single supposedly identical definition.

records.title: Compatibility of results needs a chosen multiplier
records.text: Comparing a difference with a chosen multiple of its standard uncertainty requires a specified measurand and covariance-aware difference uncertainty.
assumptions: A multiplier and its intended interpretation are declared.
limitations: Compatibility is not proof of equality or an automatic product-conformity decision.

records.title: A quantity value includes its unit
records.text: A measurement value is represented by a numerical value and a unit; the stated absolute uncertainty uses that same unit.
assumptions: The quantity being reported is identified.
limitations: Numerical values in different units cannot be compared directly.

records.title: Dimensions alone do not identify a quantity
records.text: Different quantity kinds can have the same dimension or unit. Dimensional agreement is necessary for many calculations, but is not a complete semantic check.
assumptions: Use the declared SI dimensional convention.
limitations: Energy and torque must not be treated as interchangeable merely because their dimensions match.

records.title: Absolute Celsius conversion differs from an interval
records.text: Celsius temperature and kelvin temperature differ by an offset; a temperature interval has the same numerical magnitude in °C and K.
assumptions: Values refer to the stated thermodynamic/Celsius scale relationship.
limitations: Do not add 273.15 to a temperature difference or its absolute uncertainty.

records.title: Cyclic and angular frequency are different quantities
records.text: Frequency in hertz and angular frequency in radians per second differ by a factor of 2π, even though both can be expressed using inverse seconds.
assumptions: The signal has a defined cycle or angular rate.
limitations: Do not relabel Hz as rad/s without conversion.

records.title: Dimension one does not remove quantity meaning
records.text: Ratios and counts with unit one still need their quantity meaning and reference basis identified.
assumptions: The numerator, denominator or counted entity is defined.
limitations: A fraction, a radian measure and a count are not interchangeable context.

records.title: Write values and units without ambiguity
records.text: Write the unit with the numerical value; column headings can use a quantity divided by its unit. A space separates a value from °C.
assumptions: SI reporting notation is used; plane-angle notation has specified exceptions.
limitations: Formatting correctness alone does not validate a measurement.

records.title: Coverage depends on uncertainty-estimate reliability
records.text: A coverage factor intended to approximate a specified probability must account for distributional conditions and the reliability of the estimated uncertainty.
assumptions: The conventional approximation and its distributional conditions apply.
limitations: The number k=2 is not a universal 95-percent guarantee.

records.title: Welch–Satterthwaite effective degrees of freedom
records.locator: B.3, equation B-1 and following independence condition
records.text: The conventional effective-degree calculation combines independent uncertainty contributions and their degrees of freedom.
assumptions: The component uncertainty estimates meet the stated statistical-independence and approximation conditions.
limitations: Do not apply this formula unmodified to a correlated-component budget; it does not by itself choose k.

records.title: Invert a fitted response model in its valid range
records.text: For a response model y=a+b*x with nonzero b, the corresponding input estimate is (y-a)/b.
assumptions: The fitted linear response is applicable at the new indication; b is nonzero.
limitations: This arithmetic does not justify extrapolation, stability or neglected calibration uncertainty.

records.title: Sensitivities of inverse linear calibration
records.text: Differentiating the linear inverse gives sensitivities to the indication, intercept and slope; propagate their complete covariance matrix.
assumptions: First-order propagation is adequate; parameter/input units are consistent.
limitations: These are locally derived derivatives, not extra measurements from the source.

records.title: Calibration must remain applicable over time
records.locator: §2.3.6.4, Lack of system control and day-to-day differences
records.text: Drift or day-specific changes can invalidate a calibration relationship. Aggregated data may hide differences visible when measurements are examined by day.
assumptions: Repeated checks concern the same specified response regime.
limitations: A certificate date alone does not establish current statistical control.

records.title: Calibration does not inherently improve precision
records.text: Bias correction through calibration is not inherently a reduction of replicate scatter; assess performance in the intended environment.
assumptions: The distinction between bias and dispersion is retained.
limitations: A smaller correction after adjustment does not prove better repeatability.

records.title: Monitor a linear calibration across its range
records.text: The cited linear-calibration procedure uses check standards near the lower, middle and upper parts of the range, with frequency informed by observed stability.
assumptions: The linear-calibration control setting of the source applies.
limitations: Three points are not a universal assurance for arbitrary nonlinear or unstable systems.

records.title: Variance of a mean with correlated inputs
records.text: For the arithmetic mean, propagation with sensitivities 1/n gives the sum of all covariance entries divided by n squared.
assumptions: The supplied covariance describes the readings; averaging is a linear model.
limitations: The familiar variance/n reduction follows only with the appropriate zero-covariance and equal-variance conditions.

records.title: A common offset does not average away
records.text: With an uncertain common offset independent of independent reading noise, averaging reduces the noise contribution but leaves the offset variance.
assumptions: Var(b)=u_b^2; Var(epsilon_i)=sigma^2; all stated independence conditions hold.
limitations: This is a model identity, not a diagnosis of a particular sensor.

records.title: Quantization uncertainty needs an explicit model
records.locator: A.5, equation A-7; local a=step/2 substitution
records.text: Assuming a uniform rounding error within half a display step gives standard uncertainty step/sqrt(12).
assumptions: Rounding, not truncation; the uniform model is justified independently of the display specification.
limitations: Resolution alone does not establish this distribution; avoid counting the same effect twice.

records.title: A zero derivative can hide nonlinear uncertainty
records.locator: A.3 first-order limit; local two-point counterexample
records.text: For equally likely X=-1,0,1 and Y=X squared, the derivative at the input mean is zero, but exact enumeration gives output mean 2/3 and variance 2/9.
assumptions: The three-point distribution and nonlinear function are declared synthetic mathematics.
limitations: This counterexample disproves universal adequacy of first-order propagation; it does not diagnose every nonlinear model.
